summary: Type-safe REST API client generation using interface-first design and modern HttpClient practices.
recommendedPatterns: Define typed HTTP interfaces rather than ad hoc request strings.
Prefer System.Text.Json unless compatibility requires Newtonsoft.
Use IHttpClientFactory where the host platform supports it.
avoidPatterns: Do not hand-roll repetitive REST clients when a typed Refit interface is a better fit.
Do not ignore response error modeling and API exception handling.
setupSteps: Create interface contracts for HTTP APIs.
Register typed clients with the host container or factory integration.
commonPitfalls: Guessing package/API names without checking Refit contracts.
Ignoring API error surfaces or serialization choices.

features: Testing helpers and opt-in reflection fallback
packageSelection: Use Refit; its source generator is the default client implementation.
Add Refit.HttpClientFactory for dependency-injected resilient HttpClient pipelines.
Add Refit.Newtonsoft.Json only when Newtonsoft-specific serialization is required.
Use Refit.Reflection only as an explicit fallback where generated factories cannot be registered, especially legacy .NET Framework cases.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Generated Refit clients are the primary choice for all statically declared service interfaces.
Do not choose reflection when the interface can be generated; reflection is an opt-in compatibility escape hatch.
compatibilityNotes: Generated clients are trimming/NativeAOT friendly when serializer models are also configured appropriately.
Response ownership/disposal differs between T, ApiResponse<T>, HttpResponseMessage, and Stream return types.
migrationGuidance: Move hand-written REST wrappers to annotated interfaces incrementally and preserve headers, serialization, cancellation, and error semantics in contract tests.
Replace reflection factory use with generated factories where supported; keep Refit.Reflection only at verified legacy boundaries.
